<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's GitHub repository using a tagged release archive over HTTPS. The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, so the integrity of the source will be verified upon download. During the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` execution, only the global scope and `pkgver()` function (if present) are evaluated — however, no `pkgver()` function is defined, so only static declarations are processed.

There are no command substitutions, dynamic sourcing, or execution of external code in the global scope. The `source` array uses a direct URL to a versioned tarball, with no obfuscation or redirection. The `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions are not executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags, so their contents are out of scope for this safety gate. No data exfiltration, network calls, or dangerous operations occur during sourcing.

This file poses no risk during the specified commands.
</details>

<details>
The PKGBUILD file follows standard Arch User Repository (AUR) packaging practices and shows no signs of malicious behavior. The build process uses `cargo` to compile the Rust-based application in a reproducible manner with `--locked`, `--frozen`, and `--target` flags, which help ensure dependency consistency and build isolation.

All operations are confined to the package build directory and the package destination (`$pkgdir`). The installed files include the binary, README, and LICENSE—typical for a well-formed package. There are no network requests during build or install, no use of `eval`, `base64`, or obfuscated commands, and no attempts to access sensitive files or exfiltrate data. The maintainer metadata is present but unremarkable.

The package depends only on standard Rust runtime libraries (`gcc-libs`) and build-time `cargo`, both expected for a Rust application. The prepare, build, check, and package functions perform routine tasks without side effects. No suspicious scripts or post-install hooks are present.
</details>
